messages:
marisa: quick heads-up — after enabling per-tenant SLO sampling the other day we started seeing a ton more "noise" in the console for tenants with bursty traffic. not sure our sampling heuristics are doing what we expect :(

jordan: copy. which heuristics are active? the rate-based one or the capacity-window one?

marisa: both. by default the console applies: 1) tenant-rate-sample (p=.01) and 2) capacity-hysteresis (10s window). but for small tenants the sample probability makes alerts jumpy.

kai: this is expected — small n => high variance. we should bias samples towards signal-heavy windows rather than uniform sampling. e.g., sample more when error rate > baseline.

liz: +1. also we don't persist the sampling decision with the alert fingerprint. two identical incidents can be sampled differently and that trips downstream dedupe.

marisa: great point. makes debugging harder. suggestion: sample key decisions hashed by (tenant_id, alert_fingerprint, bucket_start) so samples are deterministic for the bucket. cheap and stable.

jordan: makes sense. downside is correlated misses if the hash falls on the unlucky side. could we add a fallback: deterministic sample + occasional forced capture for one in N buckets?

kai: yes — deterministic for normal flow, and a forced capture every M minutes per tenant to keep coverage. M configurable via console policy.

liz: we need an API shape for this. current notify-sampling is boolean + rate. propose new payload in /api/v1/slo-sampling PATCH: {"mode":"deterministic","p":0.01,"force_every_s":3600} — backward compatible if mode omitted.

marisa: liking this. UX question: in the console should we show effective sample rate and an example of which alerts are being dropped? teams ask for explainability.

jordan: show a small preview: given current traffic, estimated rows retained / hour and a few recent example hashes (anonymized). also surface when deterministic hashing will always drop a fingerprint (edge case).

kai: telemetry: emit slo.sampling.effective_rate{tenant,mode} gauge and slo.sampling.example_kept (log line) with hashed fingerprint so we can debug without PII.

liz: alerting API change needs migration plan. make server accept both old bool and new object. roll out in two phases: 1) accept new payload, 2) UI exposes mode, 3) deprecate old field after 6 weeks.

marisa: rollouts UX: add a per-tenant preview panel with toggle to simulate "force capture" for 10 buckets so customer can sanity-check. keep feature behind flag for first few accounts.

jordan: can someone open a small RFC PR with config schema + metric names? I'll attach it to the console epic.

marisa: i'll draft the PR. quick todo: Kai — sketch sampling deterministic hash formula. Liz — draft API compatibility notes. Jordan — add preview mockups in the PR description. i'll wire the feature flag.

kai: on it. formula: sha256(tenant|fingerprint|floor(ts/window)) -> uint64 then compare to p*2^64. will write test vectors.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: bench/sampling-test -> staging (link: https://ci.redwood/bench/sampling-test/42) :rocket:

marisa: thx — i'll watch the staging run and post results.

sai: fyi — observed a tenant where effective_rate dropped from 1.0 -> 0.005 after rollout because their fingerprint namespace was high-entropy. deterministic will help but we should also surface that to them.

marisa: good catch. i'll add an "alertability" score to the preview so we can warn when a tenant's dedupe/fingerprint strategy interacts poorly with sampling.

liz: cool. PR when ready and i'll schedule compatibility announcement in #release-war-room. :+1:
